record.tooling: KVM with autoinstall for Hestia CP, VestaCP and Plesk; the page advertises instant setup by email. No API was read.
record.chaining: 2 GB of RAM, 30 GB of SSD and 2 TB of transfer for EUR 5, with a US east coast, a US west coast and a Moldovan location at one price (the S1 cart offers USA (New York), Moldova and USA (Oregon); no Romania). It is the node to put a crawler queue, a small database or a scheduler on; the 30 GB disk rules out any archive role.

limits.value: 2 TB a month on a 1 Gbps shared port. The port is shared rather than guaranteed, so a sustained daytime pull competes with neighbours before the 2 TB counter matters, and the 30 GB disk caps any local working set long before either.

record.notes: The page prints the euro sign; every figure here is spelled EUR to keep the strings ASCII. No free tier was read, so the verdict stays paid-only. Two billing facts on the page are not a free tier and stay here rather than promoted: 'Make an annually order and pay only 10 months', which is two months of service free on an annual term, and a 'FREE TRIAL WINDOWS' note that refers to a 180-day Windows licence trial, not to the server. The vendor's homepage advertises the NVMe line separately, so the EUR 5 plan is the SSD line, not the NVMe line. The traffic add-on's price, formerly unsettled, is now in egress.price_per_tb from the cart.
